issues.description: The lock-freedom predicate existentially chooses one thread for the entire leads-to relation, so an out-of-set thread makes the property vacuously true even when a real thread waits forever.
issues.rationale: Tid is int and inv_unchanged fixes ProcSet to [0,n). Choose i=-1: in_ProcSet(i) is false at every suffix, so always(trying(i) implies eventually(any_cs)) holds vacuously. Thus the old existential predicate holds on every execution with that fixed process set, regardless of progress. A constant trace with ProcSet={0}, pc[0]=lock and no cs state satisfies the old predicate using i=-1, whereas the repaired predicate (exists i trying(i)) leads_to (exists j cs(j)) is false. This is a counterexample to the adequacy of the specification, not a claim that such a nonprogress trace satisfies the program transition/fairness assumptions. The bad formula was introduced by PR commit706e8dc268643ba8808b0621f497b24053fe640e (originally valid_tid) and survives at this pre-repair snapshot; the direct child moves the existential inside the antecedent.
issues.source_evidence:
227: pub open spec fn dead_and_alive_lock_free() -> TempPred<ProgramState> {
